record.paper_title: Some open problems about aspherical closed manifolds
record.original_question: Let M be an aspherical closed orientable manifold with vanishing simplicial volume ||M|| = 0. Must its universal cover M̃ be of determinant class, and must all of its L²-Betti numbers vanish while its L²-torsion also vanishes; that is, b_p^(2)(M̃) = 0 for all p >= 0 and ρ^(2)(M̃) = 0?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let M be an aspherical closed orientable manifold, and let M̃ denote its universal cover, viewed as a free, proper, cocompact action of π₁(M) on M̃. Recall:

• The simplicial volume ‖M‖ is the infimum of ∑|aᵢ| over all real singular cycles ∑aᵢσᵢ representing the fundamental class [M] ∈ Hₙ(M;ℝ).

• The p-th L²-Betti number bₚ^{(2)}(M̃) is defined via the von Neumann dimension dim_{𝒩(π₁(M))} of the reduced L²-homology of M̃ with respect to the group von Neumann algebra 𝒩(π₁(M)).

• M̃ is said to be of determinant class if, for every p, the Fuglede–Kadison determinant of the p-th combinatorial Laplacian on the L²-chain complex of M̃ (with respect to any equivariant smooth triangulation) is well defined and nonzero in the appropriate sense.

• When M̃ is of determinant class, its L²-torsion ρ^{(2)}(M̃) ∈ ℝ is the alternating sum (with appropriate signs) of the logarithms of these Fuglede–Kadison determinants.

Prove or disprove: If ‖M‖ = 0, then M̃ is of determinant class, bₚ^{(2)}(M̃) = 0 for all p ≥ 0, and ρ^{(2)}(M̃) = 0.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a well-known conjecture (Conjecture 0.17 in Lück's "L²-Invariants" book) relating vanishing simplicial volume to the vanishing of L²-Betti numbers and L²-torsion for aspherical closed manifolds. It remains open in general; only partial results are known (e.g., Gromov's strategy via Gaboriau theory, Sauer's results on volume and L²-Betti numbers, and gap/vanishing theorems for small minimal volume).
